sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a house in Akron, Ohio?
sections.html:
Akron sits in Summit County, and the county bills the tax through its Fiscal Office. One elected fiscal officer runs three divisions there: the Auditor values property, the Treasurer collects and chases late payments, and the Recorder files deeds.

The office announced a temporary move out of the Ohio Building at 175 S. Main St. while that building is renovated, with the stay described as lasting until late 2026. Check the fiscal office site for the counter address before any in-person trip.

sections.h2: When is the second-half Akron property tax due?
sections.html:
Summit County collects real estate tax in two halves, with the second half due in July. For the second half of 2025, bills went out starting June 24, 2026, later than in earlier years, and the closing date for payment was Friday, July 31, 2026. The fiscal office tied the delay to Ohio House Bill 186, which created an Inflation Cap Credit for taxpayers in certain school districts that sit on the 20-mill floor and for joint vocational districts on the 2-mill floor, and which forced a one-time recalculation of rates.

The same notice says a payment mailed in must carry a U.S. postmark on or before the due date to avoid the statutory 10 percent late penalty, and a private postage meter does not count. Ohio law puts the duty on the owner to get and pay the bill, so call 330-643-2588 for a copy if one does not arrive.

sections.h2: What ways can you pay an Akron tax bill?
sections.html:
The Summit County notice lists four routes:

  • In person at the Treasurer Division counter.
  • By mail, with the postmark rule above.
  • Online or by phone through ACI Payments, with a service fee for cards and a $1 fee for e-checks. Have the parcel number ready.
  • At participating banks in the Regional Tax Collection System. The branch must be in Summit County, and not every bank takes cash.

Owners who cannot pay in full can use the Tax Installment Program if all taxes and assessments are current and the parcel is owner-occupied; the number to enroll is (330) 643-2869. Separately, the Real Estate Discount program lets a taxpayer pay toward a half in monthly coupons and earn a credit based on county investment yield. Enrollment runs July 1 to October 31 for the first half and January 1 to March 31 for the second half, and taxes must be current. Military reservists on active duty can defer taxes; the number for that application is (330) 643-2641.

sections.h2: What if the Akron tax is already delinquent?
sections.html:
Summit County's Delinquent Tax Payment Plan, started in 1987, lets an owner who missed a first or second half payment set up monthly installments. Once the plan begins, the delinquent balance is frozen in a special account with no further interest, and the extra interest is abated when the plan is completed. The owner must still pay current taxes as they come due. The Delinquent Tax Department is at 330-643-2600.

The county's Tax Certificate Liens page warns that to avoid a sale of a tax certificate lien on a parcel, the taxes must be paid in full or a payment plan arranged, and that fees and costs of a certificate sale may fall on the owner. Ask the Treasurer Division for a payoff figure before the closing date so the title company can include it.

sections.h2: How do you contest an Akron home value?
sections.html:
The Summit County Board of Revision hears complaints about value. Forms are accepted from January 1 to March 31, by U.S. Mail postmarked by the deadline, in person, or online through the county's Smartfile system. Questions go to bor@summitoh.net or 330-926-2559.

  • The board's members are the fiscal officer, the county executive and the clerk of courts, or their representatives.
  • Filing starts a legal proceeding, and the owner carries the burden of proof with supporting documents.
  • The board does not hear complaints about the tax itself, only the valuation.

The official page adds that Ohio law calls for a reappraisal every six years with an update in the third year. New construction is added at cost, though routine upkeep such as a new roof does not raise the appraisal while structural work on wiring, plumbing, framing or foundation may.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can an Akron homeowner use?
sections.html:
The fiscal office describes the Homestead Exemption as removing the first $29,000 of appraised value from taxation for a single-family home, with an average saving of $535 a year. Eligible veterans with a 100 percent service-connected disability rating get an extra exemption on the first $58,000. Applicants over 65 or permanently and totally disabled must stay under a household income cap, listed as $40,000 for 2025 applications and $41,000 for 2026, and the information line is (330) 643-2661.

The owner-occupancy credit lowers the tax charged by qualified levies on a principal residence. The office asks for applications by December 31 of the year you qualify, rental properties are ineligible, and the reduction stays only until the property transfers or stops being the owner's residence. Because of that, ask the fiscal office what credits your parcel currently has before you list it.

sections.h2: What fees apply when an Akron house changes hands?
sections.html:
The county's Property Transfer Department approves the legal description and conveyance, and it accepts DTE Form 100, the statement of value and receipt, plus DTE Form 100 (EX) for exempt transfers. The page asks for properly prepared forms by 3:30 p.m. for same-day transfer of title, citing ORC 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3).

Summit County Fiscal Office fees for a property transfer, as printed on its fee page
ItemFee printed by the office
Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1000, rounded up to the next $100 of the sale price
Lot fee50 cents per lot in the legal description, exempt or not
Basic recording$34.00 for 2 pages, $8.00 each added page
Non-compliant document$20.00 per document
Cross reference$4.00 each

Whether the seller or the buyer pays each item is a matter for the purchase contract, so ask the title company how it will split them on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What should an owner know about Akron itself?
sections.html:
Akron lies about 39 miles south of Lake Erie on the Glaciated Allegheny Plateau, bordered by Cuyahoga Falls on the north and Barberton to the southwest. The Ohio and Erie Canal runs through the city and splits east from west. The town was laid out in December 1825 at the summit of that canal, the name coming from the Greek word for summit, and it became the Summit County seat in 1841 and a city in 1865. Tire makers made it the Rubber Capital of the World, and Goodyear Heights and Firestone Park were built as company neighborhoods for rubber workers. Kenmore was annexed in 1928.

The economy leans on health care, higher education and polymers. Top employers listed in the city's 2020 financial report include Summa Health System, the University of Akron, Akron Children's Hospital, FirstEnergy, Akron General and Akron Public Schools. Public school students attend the Akron City School District, which is partway through a 15-year, $800 million rebuilding program.

  • Population: 189,691 in July 2025, down 0.4 percent from the April 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 50.7 percent, against 67.5 percent for Summit County.
  • Median owner-occupied value: $122,000, compared with $208,700 countywide.
  • Median household income: $48,076; median gross rent: $955.
  • Land area: 61.93 square miles, about 3,075 residents per square mile in 2020.

The figures come from Census QuickFacts. With about half of Akron's homes rented, a seller with a tenant in place should settle the lease question before listing.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Akron property tax to?
faqs.a: You pay the Summit County Fiscal Office, Treasurer Division. The City of Akron sits inside Summit County, and the county bills and collects the tax.

faqs.q: What was the due date for second-half 2025 Akron property tax?
faqs.a: It was Friday, July 31, 2026, with bills mailed beginning June 24, 2026. Mailed payments had to carry a U.S. postmark by that date to avoid the 10 percent penalty.

faqs.q: When can I file a Board of Revision complaint in Akron?
faqs.a: Forms are accepted from January 1 through March 31, by mail with a postmark by the deadline, in person, or online through Smartfile. Call 330-926-2559 with questions.

faqs.q: What is the conveyance fee when I sell in Akron?
faqs.a: The Fiscal Office prints $4.00 per $1000, rounded up to the next $100 of the sale price, plus a 50 cent lot fee for each lot in the legal description.

faqs.q: What can I do about delinquent property tax in Akron?
faqs.a: Call the Delinquent Tax Department at 330-643-2600 about the Delinquent Tax Payment Plan. It freezes the balance with no further interest while you pay it in monthly installments and keep current taxes paid.
